contractChangeReason: The required on-foot approach and physical-W arrival are already signed. Re-entering departure boarding on the actual Origin surface contradicts that lifecycle. However, v2 return:origin binds only exact flight/landing workOrder and an actionable flight verb at every state, so selecting that ID alone cannot truthfully guide the on-foot interval. Explicitly bind disembark/on-foot copy in the same objective; no new plot, player verb, objective, beat, anchor or milestone is required.

lifecycleRequirements: Before departure and wherever continuing the trip actually requires boarding or lifting outside the reached Origin approach, retain existing board/launch controls and their real readiness; this proposal does not broaden or replace those controls.

Keep return:origin during flight/descent and the complete grounded Origin approach, with the exact conditional copy for actual flight-control versus embodied state. A mere controlMode change to fps on Origin must not re-enter departure boarding.

Resolve one real Origin/audit-site destination; once on foot it must lead toward physical W, not the hatch. Preserve mounted-target readiness and existing destination ownership through the real world handoff; no zero-coordinate marker, fabricated actor or second marker language.
Existing disembarkation owns its actual control/input transition; no new key, F task or automatic grant is introduced. Already embodied arrival skips the disembark copy naturally.

Only real grounded Origin, embodied approach and physical W reach earn origin-landed once and clear return guidance. Select the existing survey objective from actual saved/current survey state; initial offer/start must still obey its real interaction and recording rules.

Same-ID phase changes silently replace standing text without another entry cue or score event. Pause/Continue must reconstruct actual arrival state, preserve earned receipts and avoid stale boarding, false missing targets or replayed arrival. Optional boarding at an actually usable hatch remains a normal action, not the chapter-required destination.
